root_cause_confirmed.class: false premise in a frozen bound; not a harness bug, not a property of the trained model
root_cause_confirmed.statement: V(tau,w)=0 holds only where the extractor is exactly translation-equivariant, which excludes a 15-feature-cell (240 px) halo at every crop edge whose source column differs between the two crops. GEOM-001's HS1 window w<54 started at w=0, inside that halo.
root_cause_confirmed.propagated_into_the_mask: GEOM-001 mask x in [64,864) = feature columns [4,54), including contaminated 4..14; there the POSITIVE cells do not correspond, so the TREATMENT was corrupted, not a nuisance term
root_cause_confirmed.why_the_design_audit_missed_it: the 477 px receptive field was derived correctly and the contamination was declared, then argued away as a main effect cancelled by the 2x2. That argument is true of the CANCELLATION and false of the ANCHOR.
root_cause_confirmed.empirical_confirmation: two different arbitrary halos flipped the GEOM-001-mask argmin in 8 of 24 cells; the corrected mask is bit-identical 24/24

geometry_source.extractor: 4 x Conv2d(k=5,s=2,p=2) [no activations] + 6 x ResBlock(32) + Conv2d(32->32,k=3,p=1)
geometry_source.shift_convention: shift_left(x,k)[w] = x[w+k]; zero fill for w >= FW-k
geometry_source.aggregation: 5 x Conv3d(3x3x3, padding=1) -> spatial radius 5 cells in (k,y,w)
geometry_source.readout: bilinear upsample (17,71)->(272,1136) align_corners=True; per-pixel z across k; softmax(-z); soft-argmin

extractor_halo_cells_measured.note: one-cell asymmetry from stride/padding parity; NOT relied upon; the adopted symmetric bound is a strict subset

derived_domain.cost_volume_binding_constraint: Lf[w+k] clean at k=11 => w <= 55-11 = 44; this is stricter than 55-tau for every tau<=6, so the domain is TAU-INDEPENDENT
derived_domain.pixel_band_derivation: align_corners: u = 70x/1135; need floor(u) >= 20 and floor(u)+1 <= 39 => x >= ceil(1135*20/70)=325 and 70x < 1135*39 => x <= 632
derived_domain.rows_derived_valid: ALL 17 feature rows (horizontal arm: both crops share rows [0,272), so row halos are identical and cancel)

corrected_mask.row_bound_provenance: INHERITED unchanged from ARCH-RATE classification_spec.json; the derivation independently shows all rows are admissible, so this border is strictly conservative. Inherited, not derived -- stated, not hidden.
corrected_mask.why_not_15_to_55_minus_tau: it would be wrong twice: TOO WIDE (ignores the k<=11 reach and the 5-cell aggregation radius) and TAU-DEPENDENT (a support shrinking with tau confounds the across-tau comparison the statistic depends on)

interaction_validity.cancellation: UNCONDITIONAL -- pointwise, content-independent, valid inside the halo and inside the zero-fill region (there every term reduces to -Rf and cancels)
interaction_validity.anchor: H1's prediction 'the minimum sits at k=tau' exists ONLY where V(tau)=0, i.e. only on the clean domain. THIS is what needed the mask.
interaction_validity.the_conflation_that_caused_the_failure: 'main effects cancel' is true and was used to justify ignoring the halo. But the halo does not introduce a main effect -- it DESTROYS THE TREATMENT in the positive cells. Cancellation protects against H2/H3; it cannot manufacture an anchor that is not there.
interaction_validity.aggregation_receptive_field: does NOT break cancellation -- under an affine aggregation the identically-zero cost interaction maps to an identically-zero aggregated interaction, receptive field and padding included (S4). The receptive field is handled by the 5-cell shrink.
interaction_validity.aggregation_own_padding: needs no exclusion -- it is part of the LINEAR operator, applied identically to all four cells, so it lives in the channel the interaction cancels exactly
interaction_validity.approximate_only_to: float32 round-off (~1.8e-07 relative), bounded by HS4 at 1e-5
